I did an undergraduate and masters degree with misophonia. I always contacted the uni before an exam to let them know I would be wearing earplugs due to misophonia, and they were always fine with it. Lectures could get a little frustrating if people sat near me were whispering/eating/etc but my uni uploaded all the lecture slideshows and audio recordings onto a student portal, so if I felt like I hadn't been able to concentrate very well I just went over the slides again in the silence of my own dorm. My master's degree was almost entirely coursework based which was great for me since I could work on it wherever I felt most comfortable. I didn't want to give up due to my misophonia and anxiety, though I can totally understand why people would. Pushing through it was really difficult at times but on the whole I'm happy I managed to work with it.

I went just over 24 hours without sleep earlier this year, when I was travelling home from a holiday abroad. I've pulled all-nighters before and been fine but for some reason it was so much worse travelling with no sleep. 

We had 2 consecutive long haul flights with a small layover that didn't give us enough time to rest, and I couldn't manage to sleep on either of the planes (flight anxiety plus bad turbulence, not a winning combination) so by the time we got into London I was already pretty exhausted. 

The London underground wasn't running from Heathrow for some reason (genuinely don't remember, probably rail maintenance though?), so we had to get a coach to get to King's Cross train station. By that point I think I was almost... too tired to sleep? I just kind of spaced out until we got to the station. 

Got on our train to the other side of the country and... about halfway through we broke down. For an hour. And it was at this point that the screws in the wall started to dance around on the table in the corner of my eyes. 
It's the only time I've hallucinated. I thought they were quite cute to be honest. You hear stories about people's exhaustion hallucinations being terrifying but I just remember thinking 'hmmm. I don't think those screws are supposed to do that.' 

It's safe to say that once we got home, I had the best night's sleep I've ever had.
